The varying widths of the 90% confidence intervals directly reflect the increasing uncertainty inherent in forecasting further into the future. As the horizon extends to 1 week, the interval widens to [104.09, 108.33], incorporating potential volatility from routine market activity, minor economic data releases, or small shifts in sentiment that can accumulate over several days. While the forecast anticipates stability, several specific risks or events could push actual outcomes beyond these stated intervals. Geopolitical developments, like new conflicts or major international policy disputes, could also introduce substantial volatility. Furthermore, unforeseen industry-specific disruptions, major technological breakthroughs, or significant "black swan" events that are difficult to predict could all lead to outcomes far outside the expected 90% range, representing the less likely but more impactful "tail risks."
